title: Exterior Painting in Alachua, FL | Stucco & Siding
description: Exterior painting in Alachua, FL built for humid summers and harsh west-wall sun: acrylic on siding, elastomeric on stucco, up to a 10-year warranty.
heroIntro: We prep and coat each side of an Alachua home based on the weather it faces, from the sun-baked west wall to the shaded side that grows mildew.

questions: When is the best season to paint a house exterior in Alachua?
Why is my west wall fading faster than the rest of the house?
What warranty comes with exterior painting?

sections.h2: Why one Alachua wall peels while another fades
body: Walk around almost any home in Alachua and you'll see it. Sun has bleached the south and west faces to a chalky pastel. The shaded north side has grown a green film. Down at ground level, the first foot of siding and the base of each door frame have gone soft from splashing rain and lawn sprinklers. That's why we photograph and price each side separately during the walkthrough instead of charging one flat rate for the whole house.

The house's location in town also matters. A storefront on Historic Main Street usually needs patient scraping and spot-priming on old trim. A newer home in Cinnamon Hills or Turkey Creek is more likely to need stucco crack repair and caulk replacement. Large-lot homes up north often have long fascia runs and outbuildings that get the same treatment as the main house.

sections.h2: Alachua siding, stucco, and bare wood: one coating each
body: Lap siding and trim are finished in 100% acrylic because that resin keeps its stretch as Alachua afternoons heat the wall and nights pull joints back together. Stucco that is creeping at fine cracks gets an elastomeric, which spans those gaps rather than cracking right along with them. Bare wood you want to keep natural takes a penetrating stain, since a surface film over damp wood tends to hold water in. Every product comes from the premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines and is named on your estimate. Expect two full coats, and a third when a dark house is going light. Wherever stucco is sprayed, a roller follows to push the paint into the texture.

sections.h2: Getting an Alachua exterior ready for paint
bullets: A soft wash with mildew treatment, and the walls left to dry fully before any primer
Flaking paint removed until the edges stay tight, shiny areas dulled with sandpaper
Moisture readings on suspect fascia and sills, with rotted boards replaced
Cut out and re-caulk every moving joint with a flexible sealant
Spot-prime bare wood and stucco cracks before the topcoat

body: We aim Alachua exteriors at the October-to-May stretch. Between June and September a storm builds three or four afternoons a week, so a summer crew arrives early, reads the dew point, and checks the radar before a lid comes off a can. Expect three to seven working days of painting on the whole house, with washing and drying on top of that. How long the new finish should then hold up is the subject of our article on how long exterior paint lasts in Florida.

Most exteriors start with a soft wash in Alachua. If you're changing colors, pair the job with an exterior color consult. Our main exterior painting page walks through the method in full. For the town overview, see painting in Alachua.

faqs.q: Can you paint my Alachua house in summer?
faqs.a: Yes, with some adjustments. A summer crew in Alachua gets going at sunrise, checks the dew point and radar through the morning, and wraps up before the afternoon storms build. If your dates can move, the October-to-May window dries paint most reliably.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted wood before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Soft trim and fascia come off and new boards go up instead of getting a coat of paint. Your written estimate lists that carpentry before anything starts.

faqs.q: How is an Alachua exterior repaint warrantied?
faqs.a: We put our exterior workmanship in writing for up to 10 years, and that sits alongside the separate product warranty from the company that made the paint.

faqs.q: Why does elastomeric paint matter for stucco?
faqs.a: Stucco develops hairline cracks as it moves. Elastomeric coatings are thick and flexible enough to bridge those small cracks, so water can't get into the wall behind them.
